analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Below zero – Risk Appetite Indicator negative as Tech dominates cross-asset moves
key_insights: Goldman's cross-asset Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.5, its lowest level since April 2025. Readings below -1, and especially near -2, have historically been useful contrarian signals. The current level is not yet negative enough to give that signal but suggests less-constrained upside for risky assets than at the end of the summer.

Tech has become a larger driver of risk appetite. The correlation between the RAI and Nasdaq 100 performance relative to the S&P 500 equal weight has risen over recent years and reached almost 1 in recent weeks.

Differences in sensitivity to Semiconductor stocks explain cross-asset performance over the past 3 weeks, more so than sensitivity to oil prices. The Dollar has also behaved in a more pro-cyclical fashion.
Credit components drove most of the RAI decline and weighed on the PC1 'Global growth' factor. The bond yield rally supported the PC2 'Monetary policy' factor.
Credit excess returns saw another multi-standard-deviation sell-off last week. G4 10y bonds rallied, providing some protection against the AI sell-off.

Most Euro Area-exposed assets underperformed their betas to global growth and monetary policy pricing, as OAT-Bund spreads widened beyond fundamentals. Last week Euro Area flash PMIs declined below expectations while US PMIs were roughly unchanged.
Within equities, defensive/quality styles and Value outperformed their growth- and policy-implied returns. This buffered broad equity markets against the Tech-driven momentum unwind.

Option markets price more uncertainty over the next 2 weeks than the subsequent month, consistent with a busy catalyst calendar. Nasdaq 100 and other equity markets price larger moves this week, when Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report. Long-dated USTs and HY credit price larger moves next week around the US mid-term elections.
Goldman's economists expect a Fed hold this week followed by a hike in December. Investors also follow the BoJ and ECB this week.

Asset allocation remains modestly pro-risk: OW Equities for 3m/12m, UW Credit for 3m/12m, OW Cash for 3m and OW Bonds for 12m. AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility, but earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end.

Forecasts: S&P 500 7624 now, 8000 at 3m, 8300 at 6m, 8700 at 12m. Gold 3,996 now, 4,715 at 3m and 5,235 at 12m, with an OW stance. WTI 110 now, 80 at 3m and 70 at 12m. Brent 117 now, 88 at 3m and 75 at 12m.
